entire_current.source_text: The image of a box is a zonotope. $W$ maps $\{\|\delta\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\}$ to a sum of segments $\varepsilon[-w_j,w_j]$ over its columns (a parallelogram for invertible $2\times2$ $W$). The tightest enclosing box has half-widths $\varepsilon\|w_{i,:}\|_1$, which is what interval bound propagation keeps: for $W=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$, $\varepsilon=1$, the image is the square with corners $(\pm2,0),(0,\pm2)$, area $8$, inside the box $[-2,2]^2$ of area $16$.

entire_proposed.source_text: The image of a box is a zonotope. For $\varepsilon>0$, $W$ maps $\{\|\delta\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\}$ to a sum of segments $\varepsilon[-w_j,w_j]$ over its columns (a parallelogram for invertible $2\times2$ $W$). The tightest enclosing box has half-widths $\varepsilon\|w_{i,:}\|_1$, which is what interval bound propagation keeps: for $W=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$, $\varepsilon=1$, the image is the square with corners $(\pm2,0),(0,\pm2)$, area $8$, inside the box $[-2,2]^2$ of area $16$.

current.source_text: Proofs. $|(Ax)_i|\le\sum_j|a_{ij}|\,\|x\|_\infty$, attained by $x_j=\mathrm{sign}(a_{i^\star j})$ for the worst row $i^\star$. $\|Ax\|_1\le\sum_j|x_j|\sum_i|a_{ij}|$, attained at $x=e_{j^\star}$. Each output coordinate $a_{i,:}x$ is bounded by $\|a_{i,:}\|_q\|x\|_p$ (Hölder, attainable). $\square$ Running example $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2\\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$: $\|A\|_1=3$, $\|A\|_\infty=4$ (at $x=(1,1)$), $\|A\|_{1\to\infty}=2$, $\|A\|_{2\to\infty}=\sqrt8$, $\|A\|_2=2\sqrt2\approx2.83$: the longest semi-axis of the ellipse $A$ makes of the unit circle (Section 5, explorer).
